subject: Addcovar forced to contain all columns of intcovar

messages.author: 3892c547f177c712
messages.subject: Addcovar forced to contain all columns of intcovar
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to use the R/qtl package to analyze a population of 5 different backcross mouse strains. I would like to use the sex of each mouse as an additive covariate, and the strain of provenience as an interactive covariate.

To this aim, I've created a 4-columns dataframe (A, B, C, D) which indicates whether each individual belongs (1) or not (0) to the A, B, C, D strain. I am not specifying the appartenence to the fifth strain, since these four variables are enough to describe the whole population.

However, when I run the scanone function, it returns the following error message:
Warning message:
In checkcovar(cross, pheno.col, addcovar, intcovar, perm.strata, :
addcovar forced to contain all columns of intcovar


The code I'm using is the following:

pop_tot = read.cross(format = "csv", file = "bc5full.csv", na.strings = "NA", genotypes = c("1", "2"))
pop_tot = calc.genoprob(pop_tot)
pop_tot.em = scanone(pop_tot, pheno.col = "RSQ_N", method = "hk", addcovar = dati_backcross[, 9], intcovar = dati_backcross[, 4:7])


Perhaps this is somehow connected with the fact that some markers are not informative in some strains, therefore they have not been genotyped (and are indicated as "NA" in the .csv file).

I would like to share a sample of my data, but I can't since it is proprietary data; however, in case the error is not interpretable with only this information I can try to edit the data a bit and/or publish only a part.

Thank you very much!


Chiara

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Addcovar forced to contain all columns of intcovar
parts:
Interactive covariates should also be included as additive covariates. scanone looks at the intcovar and addcovar, and if there's a column in intcovar that's not in addcovar, it adds it to addcovar and issues the warning.

You can ignore the warning, or you can make addcovar = (sex, strain) and intcovar = (strain). The results should be the same, but you won't get the warning.

A warning indicates a possible problem that may be ignorable. An error indicates a definite problem; you won't get any results.

karl
